title: Kept from the Hour: Biblical Evidence for the Pretribulational Return of Christ
author: Gerald B. Stanton
summary: A classic defence of the pre-tribulation rapture, arguing from the promise of Revelation 3:10 and the nature of the tribulation as divine wrath.

title: A Systematic Theology of the Christian Religion
author: J. Oliver Buswell Jr.
summary: Two-volume systematic theology whose eschatology section argues for a rapture at the seventh, or last, trumpet in the middle of the seventieth week.

title: The Sign
author: Robert Van Kampen
summary: Full statement of the prewrath system, arguing that the church is gathered after the cosmic signs and before the day of the Lord.

title: The Approaching Advent of Christ
author: Alexander Reese
summary: A detailed posttribulational critique of the Darby school, arguing that the early church and the New Testament know only one coming after the tribulation.

title: The Saints' Rapture to the Presence of the Lord Jesus
author: Robert Govett
summary: A statement of the partial-rapture view, arguing that only watchful believers are taken before the tribulation.

title: Two Academical Exercises on Subjects Bearing the Following Titles: Millennium, Last-Novelties
author: Morgan Edwards
summary: Essay by a colonial Baptist pastor that places the rapture of the saints about three and a half years before the end; cited by pretribulationists as an early witness.

title: The Coming of Messiah in Glory and Majesty
author: Manuel Lacunza (as Juan Josafat Ben-Ezra); translated by Edward Irving
summary: A Jesuit futurist premillennial work that revived expectation of a literal reign of Christ and was translated by Edward Irving.

title: The Rapture and an Early Medieval Citation
author: Timothy J. Demy and Thomas D. Ice
summary: Bibliotheca Sacra article presenting the Pseudo-Ephraem sermon as an early pre-tribulational statement; its reading is disputed by other scholars.

title: The Incredible Cover-Up
author: Dave MacPherson
summary: Argues that the pre-tribulation rapture originated with Margaret MacDonald in 1830 and was taken up by Darby and Irving; the claim is disputed by pretribulationists and many historians.

title: The Roots of Fundamentalism: British and American Millenarianism, 1800-1930
author: Ernest R. Sandeen
summary: Standard history of nineteenth-century millenarianism, including Albury, Irving, Darby, the Niagara conferences and the Scofield Bible.

title: Maranatha: Our Lord, Come! A Definitive Study of the Rapture of the Church
author: Renald E. Showers
summary: A dispensational defense of the pretribulation rapture, with extended treatment of imminence and the day of the Lord.

title: The End: Re-thinking the Revelation
author: Norman B. Harrison
summary: An early twentieth-century case for a rapture at the middle of the seventieth week, linked to the seventh trumpet.

title: The Sign
author: Robert Van Kampen
summary: A detailed presentation of the prewrath rapture view, distinguishing the great tribulation from the day of the Lord's wrath.

title: Entrance into the Kingdom: Reward According to Works
author: Robert Govett
summary: A Victorian English writer's case that entry into the millennial kingdom and the first rapture are rewards for faithful believers.
note: Original title and date vary across editions.

title: Firstborn Sons: Their Rights and Risks
author: G. H. Lang
summary: A Brethren writer's argument for a selective rapture of watchful believers as firstborn heirs.

title: Die Einholung des Kyrios
author: Erik Peterson
summary: A German study arguing that apantesis reflects the formal civic welcome and escort of a visiting ruler.

title: Hellenistic Formal Receptions and Paul's Use of APANTESIS in 1 Thessalonians 4:17
author: Michael R. Cosby
summary: Argues in the Bulletin for Biblical Research that apantesis was not a technical term for a formal reception.

title: A Brief Note on "Hellenistic Formal Receptions and Paul's Use of APANTESIS in 1 Thessalonians 4:17"
author: Robert H. Gundry
summary: A reply to Cosby defending the escort sense of apantesis in 1 Thessalonians 4:17.

title: Premillennialism: Why There Must Be a Future Earthly Kingdom of Jesus
author: Michael J. Vlach
summary: A short defence of a future earthly kingdom of Christ, arguing from the Old Testament promises, the Gospels, Acts and Revelation 20 that the kingdom has a future stage on this earth after Christ's return.

title: The Millennial Maze: Sorting Out Evangelical Options
author: Stanley J. Grenz
summary: A survey of the main millennial views, their history and the outlook on the world each one tends to produce, written for a general Christian readership.

title: A Basic Guide to Eschatology: Making Sense of the Millennium
author: Millard J. Erickson
summary: A revised edition of Erickson's Contemporary Options in Eschatology, setting out the millennial and tribulational views with their arguments and difficulties.

title: The Greek Testament, vol. 4 (Hebrews to Revelation)
author: Henry Alford
summary: A classic critical commentary on the Greek New Testament. Its note on Revelation 20:4-6 argues that the first resurrection must be bodily if the second is, an argument still cited by premillennialists.

title: Remarks on the Prophetic Visions in the Book of Daniel
author: Samuel Prideaux Tregelles
summary: A futurist study of Daniel by a Brethren-linked biblical scholar who rejected the secret rapture. It proposes reading Daniel 12:2 as describing two groups raised at different times.
note: First published in the 1840s-1850s in several editions; the edition year is approximate.

title: The Politics of Jesus
author: John Howard Yoder
summary: Argues that Jesus' life and cross set out a social ethic of nonviolent, servant community, so the church itself is the visible sign of God's kingdom.

title: Resident Aliens: Life in the Christian Colony
author: Stanley Hauerwas and William H. Willimon
summary: Calls the church a colony of heaven within a foreign culture; its first social task is to be a faithful community, not to manage society.

title: Living in God's Two Kingdoms: A Biblical Vision for Christianity and Culture
author: David VanDrunen
summary: Sets out a Reformed two-kingdoms view: Christians serve in the common kingdom under the Noahic covenant, while the redemptive kingdom is expressed now in the church.

title: Lectures on Calvinism (Stone Lectures)
author: Abraham Kuyper
summary: Kuyper's Princeton lectures present Calvinism as a life-system touching religion, politics, science and art, under Christ's lordship over every sphere.

title: Reformed Dogmatics, Volume 4: Holy Spirit, Church, and New Creation
author: Herman Bavinck (ed. John Bolt)
summary: Bavinck's dogmatics, translated into English; the eschatology section teaches that grace restores nature and that the new creation renews, not replaces, this world.

title: Creation Regained: Biblical Basics for a Reformational Worldview
author: Albert M. Wolters
summary: A short Kuyperian account of creation, fall and redemption: redemption restores the whole created order, so every area of life can be reformed.

title: The Institutes of Biblical Law
author: Rousas John Rushdoony
summary: A commentary on the Ten Commandments arguing that God's law, including its case laws, is the standard for personal and social life.

title: Theonomy in Christian Ethics
author: Greg L. Bahnsen
summary: Argues from Matthew 5:17-19 that the Old Testament law continues in exhaustive detail unless the New Testament changes it, including for civil rulers.

title: Unconditional Surrender: God's Program for Victory
author: Gary North
summary: A popular introduction to Christian Reconstruction: God's sovereignty, law, and the progressive victory of the gospel in history.

title: Dominion! How Kingdom Action Can Change the World
author: C. Peter Wagner
summary: Wagner argues that God commissioned believers to take dominion and transform society, naming the 'seven mountains' of culture as the arenas of that work.

title: Invading Babylon: The 7 Mountain Mandate
author: Lance Wallnau and Bill Johnson
summary: Presents the seven mountains (religion, family, education, government, media, arts and entertainment, business) as spheres believers are called to influence.

title: A New Apostolic Reformation? A Biblical Response to a Worldwide Movement
author: R. Douglas Geivett and Holly Pivec
summary: An evangelical critique of NAR teaching on present-day apostles and prophets and on the dominion or seven mountains mandate.

title: To Change the World: The Irony, Tragedy, and Possibility of Christianity in the Late Modern World
author: James Davison Hunter
summary: A sociologist argues that evangelical, mainline and Anabaptist strategies for 'changing the world' misread how culture changes, and proposes 'faithful presence' instead.

title: Whatever Happened to Heaven?
author: Dave Hunt
summary: A pretribulational critique of dominion, reconstruction and Kingdom Now teaching, warning that hope has shifted from Christ's return to earthly success.

title: The Kingdom of Christ: The New Evangelical Perspective
author: Russell D. Moore
summary: Traces how covenant and dispensational theologians moved toward an 'already and not yet' kingdom, and what this means for evangelical public engagement.

title: Christ and Culture
author: H. Richard Niebuhr
summary: A classic typology of five Christian stances toward culture, from 'Christ against culture' to 'Christ the transformer of culture'.
